You previously mentioned that the tool library was also slow when tested locally. When you performed that test, was Mastercam actually configured to use the  library from your local C: drive, or had you simply copied the file locally?  &nbsp; We tried both copying the Mill_inch.tooldb locally and pointing the File usage Mill Tool Library to the new location which seemed to have the same behavior. When  the Shared Mastercam folder was copied to the local drive and pointed to the new location it did help with the slowness. [Inline image name: image007.png] &nbsp; 2. Does the slowdown occur primarily when opening Tool Manager and selecting standard drill and tap sizes, or do you experience similar delays when creating and editing other tool types? &nbsp; Both when opening tool manager its slow and when editing its slow even when creating a new tooldb but it is still pulling the master list from the existing tool  library and causing slowness. When we selected custom tool in a blank library it was much faster. It seems the drills have some default tools that it is trying to pull from the db file when its used and still has the slowness issue. &nbsp; 3. Have you tested this behavior using a completely new, blank Mastercam file, or have your tests been performed using existing programs? &nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp; Yes, it’s been tested with a blank Mastercam file same behavior. &nbsp; 4. Could you also confirm with your IT department whether the server named HB-AD01 is a Windows server hosted in Azure or a local server connected to Azure storage? HB-AD01 is a Windows Server hosted in Azure. &nbsp; I am unable to attach the zip file from the Proc Monitor capture since it is too large. I've been reviewing the system diagnostics and network configuration information we've collected, and I'm preparing to discuss my findings with  our technical team here at Mastercam. &nbsp; Before doing so, I'd like to clarify a few things that may help us narrow down the cause. &nbsp; 1. You previously mentioned that the tool library was also slow when tested locally. When you performed that test, was Mastercam actually configured to use the library from your local C: drive, or had you simply copied the file locally? &nbsp; 2. Does the slowdown occur primarily when opening Tool Manager and selecting standard drill and tap sizes, or do you experience similar delays when creating and editing other tool types? &nbsp; 3. Have you tested this behavior using a completely new, blank Mastercam file, or have your tests been performed using existing programs? &nbsp; 4. Could you also confirm with your IT department whether the server named HB-AD01 is a Windows server hosted in Azure or a local server connected to Azure storage? &nbsp; If possible, I'd also appreciate a compressed copy of your Mill_Inch.tooldb library so I can examine the actual database. &nbsp; I'm particularly interested in understanding whether the delays are related to network file access, the tool database itself, or another component of Mastercam. &nbsp; There's no need to change anything in your current configuration. &nbsp; &nbsp; From: Mastercam Support &lt;cases@mastercam.com&gt; Sent: Monday, October 26, 2026 9:31 AM To: ryanr@hbindustries.net Cc: Lance Harding &lt;lharding@iatechgroup.com&gt; Subject: Case Number 00134446 - Mastercam Tool Manager Performance Issues on Azure Network [  ] &nbsp; CAUTION: This email originated  from outside of your organization. &nbsp; &nbsp; [Inline image URL: https://d2hqlhbe1d8j2s.cloudfront.net/mastercam/logo_v-128de24ab4db473eacfe03677b17f7ab.png?ver=1764695329565%22] &nbsp; Ryan and Lance, &nbsp; I've been continuing to investigate the Mastercam Tool Manager performance issues and wanted to share another diagnostic approach that may help us identify the underlying cause. &nbsp; One possibility I'm looking into is network latency rather than network bandwidth. Our earlier testing showed communication delays between 12 and 19 milliseconds when accessing your server. &nbsp; Although those numbers are reasonable, applications like Mastercam's Tool Manager may perform numerous individual file requests, potentially hundreds, when accessing tool libraries and related resources. If those requests are processed sequentially, even small  delays can accumulate and significantly affect performance. &nbsp; I'd like to determine whether that's what we're experiencing. &nbsp; Microsoft provides a free diagnostic utility called Process Monitor that records file system activity, including how long individual operations take. &nbsp; Here's what I'd like you to do: &nbsp; 1. Download Process Monitor from Microsoft:  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/procmon 2. Extract the ZIP file and run Procmon64.exe as Administrator. 3. Press Ctrl+E to stop the initial capture, then Ctrl+X to clear the existing events. 4. With Mastercam already running, press Ctrl+E to begin recording. 5. Open Tool Manager and reproduce the slowdown, particularly when creating a drill or tap and selecting a standard size. 6. Once the delay occurs, return to Process Monitor and press Ctrl+E to stop recording. 7. Select File &gt; Save, choose All Events, and save the capture in the native PML format. 8. Compress the PML file into a ZIP and upload it to our support case. Please also note approximately how long the operation took. &nbsp; Lance, if you're able to assist Ryan with collecting this information, I'd appreciate it. &nbsp; This capture should help us determine whether Mastercam is spending time waiting for responses from the network or whether the delay is occurring elsewhere in the application. &nbsp; There's no need to change any network or Mastercam settings for this test. &nbsp; I appreciate your assistance. I'm continuing to research this issue and would like to review the findings with our technical team here at Mastercam. &nbsp; Thank you both.  &nbsp; John Bettencourt&nbsp;/ Application engineer II  Direct: 1-206-970-5172  FOR MASTERCAM TECHNICAL SUPPORT  Create a case online at  https://my.mastercam.com/case-creation-form/ &lt;https://my.mastercam.com/case-creation-form/&gt; Email Support:  west.support@mastercam.com &lt;mailto:west.support@mastercam.com&gt;  Phone Support: (888) 396-4834 Business Hours: 6:00am – 5:00pm PT  &nbsp; &nbsp; [Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/Facebook.png] &lt;https://www.facebook.com/Mastercam/&gt;[Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/Instagram.png] &lt;https://www.instagram.com/mastercam/&gt;[Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/LinkedIn.png] &lt;https://www.linkedin.com/company/cnc-software&gt;[Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/Twitter.png] &lt;https://twitter.com/Mastercam&gt;[Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/Youtube.png] &lt;https://www.youtube.com/mastercam&gt; Mastercam West West.Support@Mastercam.com &lt;mailto:West.Support@Mastercam.com&gt; (888) 396-4834   www.mastercam.com &lt;https://www.mastercam.com&gt; Privacy Statement &lt;https://www.mastercam.com/legal/privacy-policy/&gt; Mastercam® is a registered trademark of CNC Software, LLC © 1983-2026. If those requests are processed sequentially, even small delays can accumulate and significantly affect performance. 									&nbsp; 									I'd like to determine whether that's what we're experiencing. 									&nbsp; 									Microsoft provides a free diagnostic utility called Process Monitor that records file system activity, including how long individual operations take. 									&nbsp; 									Here's what I'd like you to do: 									&nbsp; 									1. Download Process Monitor from Microsoft: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/procmon 									2. Extract the ZIP file and run Procmon64.exe as Administrator. 									3. Press Ctrl+E to stop the initial capture, then Ctrl+X to clear the existing events. 									4. With Mastercam already running, press Ctrl+E to begin recording. 									5. Open Tool Manager and reproduce the slowdown, particularly when creating a drill or tap and selecting a standard size. 									6. Once the delay occurs, return to Process Monitor and press Ctrl+E to stop recording. 									7. Select File &gt; Save, choose All Events, and save the capture in the native PML format. 									8. Compress the PML file into a ZIP and upload it to our support case. I'm continuing to investigate the Mastercam performance issues you're experiencing. I've been reviewing the system diagnostics and network configuration information we've collected, and I'm preparing to discuss my findings with our technical team here at Mastercam. 									&nbsp; 									Before doing so, I'd like to clarify a few things that may help us narrow down the cause. 									&nbsp; 									1. You previously mentioned that the tool library was also slow when tested locally. When you performed that test, was Mastercam actually configured to use the library from your local C: drive, or had you simply copied the file locally? 									&nbsp; 									2. Does the slowdown occur primarily when opening Tool Manager and selecting standard drill and tap sizes, or do you experience similar delays when creating and editing other tool types? 									&nbsp; 									3. Have you tested this behavior using a completely new, blank Mastercam file, or have your tests been performed using existing programs? 									&nbsp; 									4. Could you also confirm with your IT department whether the server named HB-AD01 is a Windows server hosted in Azure or a local server connected to Azure storage? 									&nbsp; 									If possible, I'd also appreciate a compressed copy of your Mill_Inch.tooldb library so I can examine the actual database. 									&nbsp; 									I'm particularly interested in understanding whether the delays are related to network file access, the tool database itself, or another component of Mastercam. 									&nbsp; 									There's no need to change anything in your current configuration. I'm simply gathering additional information to help make our investigation more productive. 									&nbsp; 									Thank you for your continued cooperation. class="preamble_custom-summary slds-hide" data-aura-rendered-by="179:73862;a">Good Morning John, &nbsp; I replied to your earlier email with everpath. Yes this seemed to resolve that problem. Thank you. I have used that post for various other 5 axis toolpaths before, and it works well. I actually never posted the program for the files I sent you, that used the generic haas post, I simply switched machines to see if the crash in machine simulation occurred using a different mach sim file. I attached an example of another file that has a similiar toolpath (operation 5) in this file is a similiar swarf tool path. It simulates correctly and the output from the post is correct and made good parts. The rotary table is a haas TRT310 serial number 912609 ver P20 The machine is a vf6ss serial# 1152979 with ngc control firmware version 1.69 Bob Hulegaard Milling Dept Manager Minimatics, Inc. 15500 Concord Circle Ste. 150 Morgan Hill, CA&nbsp; 95037 Phone: 650-969-5630 Mobile 408-476-6161 Fax: 408-496-0111 Email:  bhulegaard@minimatics.com &lt;mailto:bhulegaard@minimatics.com&gt; www.minimatics.com &lt;https://url.emailprotection.link/?blLw7zBZQ3RLEVS3ZV5S0AFqsOdyTJ66e4drX9ABRlWiO7aM3lJmYSgxHOndUSj6CD1nuPuQKPv3dPP9lUnFEHg~~&gt; From: Mastercam Support &lt;cases@mastercam.com&gt; Sent: Tuesday, October 27, 2026 6:58 AM To: Bob Hulegaard &lt;bhulegaard@minimatics.com&gt; Subject: Case Number 00136621 - EVERPATH Error, Mastercam Freezing &amp; Swarf Simulation [  ] &nbsp; &nbsp; [Inline image URL: https://d2hqlhbe1d8j2s.cloudfront.net/mastercam/logo_v-128de24ab4db473eacfe03677b17f7ab.png?ver=1764695329565%22] &nbsp; Bob, &nbsp; I've finished reviewing the NC files you provided and comparing the output from your Postability post against the generic Haas post. &nbsp; The Postability post uses G234 Tool Center Point Control along with G254/G255 Dynamic Work Offset commands, while the generic Haas post uses a different compensation method. 									&nbsp; 									Bob, 									&nbsp; 									I've finished reviewing the NC files you provided and comparing the output from your Postability post against the generic Haas post. 									&nbsp; 									The Postability post uses G234 Tool Center Point Control along with G254/G255 Dynamic Work Offset commands, while the generic Haas post uses a different compensation method. The resulting machine movements are significantly different, which could explain why the Postability output causes a collision during simulation. 									&nbsp; 									Based on my findings, this appears to be related to the post processor or machine configuration rather than the swarf toolpath itself. 									&nbsp; 									My recommendation is to have our Post Processing team evaluate your Postability post and make any necessary corrections. I can initiate that process for you. 									&nbsp; 									To help move things forward, please confirm the exact Haas machine model, rotary configuration, and control version. Also, let me know whether this post has successfully run other simultaneous 5-axis programs on your machine and whether the collision occurs only in simulation or has also been observed at the machine. 									&nbsp; 									I already have the files you provided, so there's no need to resend them unless our Post Processing team requests additional information. 									&nbsp; 									Also, please let me know whether installing the updated EVERPATH beta resolved the startup error and whether you've had any further freezing or crashing issues after completing the graphics driver and configuration troubleshooting. 									&nbsp; 									Once I have your feedback, we can determine the next steps for the post review and address any remaining issues. 									&nbsp; 									Thank you. 									&nbsp; 									 									John Bettencourt&nbsp;/ Application engineer II Direct: 1-206-970-5172 FOR MASTERCAM TECHNICAL SUPPORT Create a case online at  https://my.mastercam.com/case-creation-form/ Email Support:  west.support@mastercam.com Phone Support: (888) 396-4834 Business Hours: 6:00am – 5:00pm PT 									&nbsp; Learn why this is important  &nbsp; [Inline image URL: https://d2hqlhbe1d8j2s.cloudfront.net/mastercam/logo_v-128de24ab4db473eacfe03677b17f7ab.png?ver=1764695329565%22] &nbsp; Bob, &nbsp; Thank you for reaching out to Mastercam Support. I've reviewed the issues you reported and would like to address them in a few steps. &nbsp; Step 1: Update EVERPATH I reproduced the exact same EVERPATH error on my computer. Older versions of EVERPATH are not compatible with Mastercam 2027 Update 1. EVERPATH Public Beta 6 or newer is required. Please use the link below to access the myMastercam Public Beta Downloads page and download EVERPATH Beta 6 or a newer compatible version. EVERPATH download &lt;https://my.mastercam.com/product-downloads/public-beta/&gt; Run the installer, which installs over your existing Mastercam 2027 Update 1 installation. Once completed, restart Mastercam and verify that the error is gone. &nbsp; Step 2: Update Your NVIDIA Graphics Driver I'd also like you to update your NVIDIA graphics driver. Even if Windows or NVIDIA reports that your driver is already up to date, please download and reinstall it directly from NVIDIA. 1. Visit https://www.nvidia.com/drivers/ 2. Select your graphics card and download the appropriate driver. 3. Run the installer and select Custom (Advanced). 4. VERY IMPORTANT: Check the box labeled "Perform a clean installation." This is an essential step because it resets the previous NVIDIA driver settings. 5. Complete the installation and restart your computer. After restarting, test Mastercam to see whether the freezing or crashing continues. &nbsp; Step 3: Reset Your Mastercam Configuration (If Necessary) If you're still experiencing freezing or crashing, please try resetting your Mastercam configuration. 1. Completely close Mastercam. 2. Open Windows File Explorer and navigate to your Documents folder. 3. Locate the folder named "My Mastercam 2027". 4. Rename it to "My Mastercam 2027 OLD". 5. Launch Mastercam 2027 again. Mastercam will automatically create a new My Mastercam 2027 folder with fresh default settings. Your original settings will remain preserved in the renamed folder. &nbsp; Step 4: Swarf Toolpath and Machine Simulation I'll be reviewing the Mastercam files you sent to investigate why your swarf toolpath produces incorrect machine movement during simulation. I'll compare your custom post and machine configuration against the generic Haas setup. &nbsp; For now, please complete the steps above and let me know whether the EVERPATH error and freezing issues have been resolved. &nbsp; Thank you for your patience. &nbsp; &nbsp; John Bettencourt&nbsp;/ Application engineer II  Direct: 1-206-970-5172  FOR MASTERCAM TECHNICAL SUPPORT  Create a case online at  https://my.mastercam.com/case-creation-form/  Email Support:  west.support@mastercam.com  Phone Support: (888) 396-4834 Business Hours: 6:00am – 5:00pm PT &nbsp; &nbsp; [Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/Facebook.png] &lt;https://www.facebook.com/Mastercam/&gt; [Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/Instagram.png] &lt;https://www.instagram.com/mastercam/&gt; [Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/LinkedIn.png] &lt;https://www.linkedin.com/company/cnc-software&gt; [Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/Twitter.png] &lt;https://twitter.com/Mastercam&gt; [Inline image URL: https://cdn.mastercam.com/content/images/Youtube.png] &lt;https://www.youtube.com/mastercam&gt; Mastercam West West.Support@Mastercam.com (888) 396-4834   www.mastercam.com &lt;https://www.mastercam.com&gt; Privacy Statement &lt;https://www.mastercam.com/legal/privacy-policy/&gt; Mastercam® is a registered trademark of CNC Software, LLC © 1983-2026. But if you'd rather give it a shot yourself, here are some instructions that I think will get you squared away. &nbsp; I'm not familiar with how your company's network and folder structure is configured, but normally Mastercam uses a Shared Mastercam directory to access files such as your operation libraries. &nbsp; Since your company has changed its network folder structure, you'll want to make sure Mastercam is pointing to the correct shared directory on your company's network. &nbsp; Here's how to update that location: &nbsp; 1. Open Mastercam 2027. 2. Go to File &gt; Configuration &gt; Files. 3. Under Data Paths, select Shared Mastercam Folder. 4. Edit the path so it points to the correct Shared Mastercam directory on your company's network. 5. Make sure you do not include any quotation marks in the directory path. 6. Click OK to save your configuration changes. 7. Restart Mastercam and check whether your operation library loads correctly. &nbsp; If you'd rather have me remote in and look at the whole situation with you, just let me know. Open Mastercam 2027. 2. Go to File &gt; Configuration &gt; Files. 3. Under Data Paths, select Shared Mastercam Folder. 4. Edit the path so it points to the correct Shared Mastercam directory on your company's network. 5. Make sure you do not include any quotation marks in the directory path. 6. Click OK to save your configuration changes. 7.
